heard: A dead star can hide inside a living giant star. To our telescopes, the host looks like an ordinary red supergiant, but gas friction drags a swallowed neutron star toward the center. Falling gas heats up to nearly 1 billion Kelvin. This intense heat creates new heavy elements deep inside the star. The star then churns these rare metals all the way to its surface. The ravenous core keeps devouring gas and growing heavier. Eventually, that hidden dead core collapses into a black hole. Nothing survives once a dead star burrows deep inside.
